ideas.risks: The weighted per-segment capacity constraint sum_c y_{i,c}/c <= B_i may break a pure network/TU representation; a flow model may exist only for monotone lows or after adding many auxiliary nodes.
ideas.summary: Reformulate iteration 19's C(z) cover LP as a release-time interval/GUB covering problem. For each useful segment i and quote level c, set rho(i,c)=min{j>i: max_{q=i+1..j} ell_q >= c} and y_{i,c}=c x_{i,c}. Then low constraints become cumulative suffix-cover constraints sum_{rho(i,c)<=j} y_{i,c} >= d_j(z); equivalently replace d_j(z) by its record envelope max_{q<=j} d_q(z). Investigate whether this is a min-cost flow, a consecutive-ones covering LP with generalized upper bounds, or a nested resource-allocation instance.
ideas.title: Release-Time Cover Reformulation
ideas.why_promising: It exposes a hidden suffix/consecutive-ones structure in the accepted unequal-low LP and could turn the scalar fixed-point D=inf{z:C(z)<=z} into an algorithmic or closed-form theorem.

ideas.risks: The formula may have many boundary regimes, especially when S1, S2 and capacities make feasibility constraints active; the final statement may be too case-heavy to be conceptually useful.
ideas.summary: Complete the two-low increasing theorem for h^M,0^{N0},ell,0^{N1},u,0^L,h with 0<ell<u<h, including all capacity-active cases. Start from the solver's non-saturated formula, then classify regimes where d1/ell>B0 or d1/ell+(d2-d1)_+/u>B0+B1 at the fixed point. For every regime, produce matching primal masses and dual weights.
ideas.title: Two-Low Active-Cap Formula
ideas.why_promising: This is the smallest complete unequal-low theorem beyond CL-049 and would provide a reliable regression target for any proposed pooling or flow rule.

ideas.risks: Naive PAVA is already suspect: the three-low regression can skip segments and use nonlocal levels. The right transformation may be nonstandard or may fail outside monotone low sequences.
ideas.summary: Analyze the CL-049 dual pressures psi_i=[max_c {c sum_{j>i, c<=m_{i,j}} alpha_j - beta(h-c)}]_+. Since the inner sums are suffix sums after rho(i,c), try to prove that optimal low-horizon weights alpha_j have a pooled/isotonic structure after scaling by beta(h/c-1). The goal is a PAVA-like or active-set algorithm for the whole one-drought LP, with exact conditions under which earlier lows bind.
ideas.title: Dual-Pressure Pooling
ideas.why_promising: A structural dual rule would convert the accepted one-drought LP from a black-box finite LP into a usable closed theorem and may explain the 68/225 and 2.91 regressions.

ideas.risks: Experiments alone do not prove anything, and generic LP solvers can hide strict-crossing or left-limit convention mistakes. The implementation must output checkable primal and dual certificates.
ideas.summary: Build an exact rational regression suite for the finite-prefix D_n LP and for the CL-049 reduced one-drought LP. Enumerate small paths with duplicate lows, zero gaps, M>1, nonmonotone lows, and repeated droughts. For each candidate rule, automatically search for counterexamples and emit primal/dual certificates.
ideas.title: Exact LP Regression Engine
ideas.why_promising: Earlier iterations lost time to a wrong 14/45 value. A certificate-producing testbed would make future pooling, additivity, and gluing claims much easier to criticize precisely.

ideas.risks: The debt may not be Markovian: later quote opportunities and horizon-specific comparators can dilute or cancel local debts in ways a finite state variable misses.
ideas.summary: Study how one-drought high debt composes across multiple droughts. Start with two-level paths containing two diluted low/high episodes, then add unequal-low droughts. Track how mass posted at low level c creates high debt (h-c)x at later high horizons, and test whether local one-drought values add, take a maximum, or interact through shared quote coordinates.
ideas.title: Repeated-Drought Debt Calculus
ideas.why_promising: The global D_n=o(n) gluing problem cannot be solved by local one-drought formulas unless their debts compose in a controlled way. This direction attacks exactly that missing mechanism.

ideas.risks: Simple separated-block separators have already failed; a positive proof must overcome the boundary-defect obstruction CL-043, while a negative construction must verify both D_n=o(n) and failure of every fixed sublinear envelope.
ideas.summary: Focus on the two-level alphabet 0<ell<h and use the accepted positive-part dual formula to either prove D_n=o(n) implies a fixed o(T)-regret envelope, or construct a diluted drought cascade separating these notions. Any proof should use resolved low surplus and future high debt, not the raw stable-high regret Q_T.
ideas.title: Two-Level Gluing Or Separator
ideas.why_promising: Two levels are the simplest nontrivial setting where the projective-consistency question remains open. A theorem or counterexample here would likely decide the shape of the full known-path characterization.
